<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **3** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/api-surface/api.json`, `packages/spec/dropped-refinements.baseline.json`, `packages/spec/export-origins/api.json`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- the SDK route bridge reached **69** of **252** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **183** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **183**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **124** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **175** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 49c6bf3d513efd3d15a82f5a54b7887563eb0439` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `66714a72aeb3e6734043cece627ba84ed4004266` — the merge of head `ce27cea1dfaba3cd3ca56c8ede2f6448505fabf2` into base `49c6bf3d513efd3d15a82f5a54b7887563eb0439`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 66714a72aeb3e6734043cece627ba84ed4004266 && git checkout 66714a72aeb3e6734043cece627ba84ed4004266
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 49c6bf3d513efd3d15a82f5a54b7887563eb0439 ce27cea1dfaba3cd3ca56c8ede2f6448505fabf2 && git checkout -B drift-repro 49c6bf3d513efd3d15a82f5a54b7887563eb0439 && git merge --no-ff ce27cea1dfaba3cd3ca56c8ede2f6448505fabf2

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 49c6bf3d513efd3d15a82f5a54b7887563eb0439
```

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `ce27cea1dfaba3cd3ca56c8ede2f6448505fabf2`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/api/protocol.zod.ts + packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.meta-types-response-schema-36887.test.ts, packages/spec/src/type-alias-convention.pin.test.ts, packages/spec/dropped-refinements.baseline.json

PR #36948 (card #36887), net diff against `main` at merge-base `3f568c1a`. Inputs read: the card body and its three comments (triage 7125404665, claim 7127426588, dev report 7129190605), the PR body and file list, the net diff, and the check-runs on this head. The remainder of the diff (`.changeset/36887-meta-types-response-schema.md`, `content/docs/references/api/protocol.mdx`, `packages/spec/api-surface/api.json`, `packages/spec/export-origins/api.json`, `scripts/engine-double-contract.pinned.json`) is the lane seat's ACCEPT at `TIER_DEFAULT`.

Check-runs on this head at the time of this record: 24 success, 10 skipped, 33 in progress, 0 failed. Concluded green and relevant here: `Check Changeset`, `Type Check · source gates`, `Spec property liveness`, `Lint · PM dispatch-gates`, `Lint · docs & code guards`, `Lint · CI, release & engine gates`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `PR-body guards`. Not concluded: `Test Core (1..10/10)`, `Type Check · workspace`, `Type Check · consumer gates`, `Type Check UI`, `Build Core`, `Lint · repo & tooling gates`. The new test's own verdict and the workspace type-check therefore carry no gate verdict yet; this record judges the design by reading, and the landing check (every PR check green) still stands in front of the merge.

### ① Derived judgments

- Public surface, widening — right. Each `entries[]` element of `GetMetaTypesResponseSchema` declares four more members: `schemaId` (string, required), `schema` (string-keyed record, optional), `form` (`FormViewSchema`, optional), `actions` (array of `ActionSchema`, optional). One new exported type, `GetMetaTypesResponseParsed` (`api-surface/api.json`, `export-origins/api.json`, one line each). No export removed or renamed.
- Served-as-declared, read in `packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-discovery-and-bases.ts` (`getMetaTypes`, both arms) — right.
  - `schemaId: singular` is written unconditionally on the registry arm and on the synthesised arm, next to `type: singular`, so required holds and "same value as `type`" holds.
  - `schema` is `toJsonSchemaSafe(...) ?? HAND_CRAFTED_SCHEMAS[singular]`, both typed `Record | undefined`; an `undefined` member is dropped by JSON, so optional is the honest spelling. The server's own `MetaTypesListingEntry` types `schema` and `form` as always present, which is looser than the runtime; the wire schema is the accurate one.
  - `form` is `TYPE_TO_FORM[singular]`, that is `METADATA_FORM_REGISTRY`: 17 types carry one, every other type (and every synthesised entry) carries none. Optional is right.
  - `actions` is spread only when `getMetadataTypeActions(singular)` is non-empty, on both arms. Optional is right.
- Doors — right. `GET /meta/types` (and its `/meta` twin) in `packages/rest/src/meta-collection-routes.ts` serve the protocol answer through `translateMetaTypesResponse`; the runtime dispatcher (`packages/runtime/src/domains/meta.ts`, `/metadata/types` and `/metadata`) serves the protocol answer unchanged, or a `types`-only fallback, which the optional `entries` already covers. Neither door adds an entry member the schema does not declare.
- Accept set, the direction the PR does not state — named, judged acceptable under `(widening)`. The schema did accept an entry with no `schemaId`, and stripped any `schema`, `form` or `actions` value unread; it now refuses an entry without `schemaId` and a `form` or `actions` that is not a `FormView` or `Action[]`. The same holds at the type level for an implementer of the published `MetadataProtocol.getMetaTypes()` interface, whose return type is `GetMetaTypesResponse`. No code in the tree parses a response with this schema (`responseSchema` in the route ledgers is a name, never a validator), the one shipping producer has always sent `schemaId`, and `entries` itself stays optional, so no working caller is refused. See N4.
- `GetMetaTypesResponseParsed` and the 888 to 887 pin move — right. ADR-0122 D2 and D3: a schema with two shapes takes `XParsed` and loses its isomorphism pin. `FormViewSchema` and `ActionSchema` carry defaults and a transform (`collapsible`, `span`, `refreshAfter`, the `requiresFeature` lowering), so the response has two shapes. The pin test's own text names this move ("it drops by one whenever a schema gains a shape and its alias gains an `XParsed`"); the alias sits beside the bare one with the house docblock, and the receipt paragraph, the case title and the section header all read 887.
- `dropped-refinements.baseline.json` — right. The 12 new sites are exactly the 8 already ledgered for `ui/Action` (`in`, `in.ai.outputSchema`, `in.onSuccess`, `in.params.element.in`, `in.preflight.fields.element`, `in.refusals.valueType`, `in.resultDialog.fields.element`, `in.texts.valueType`) under `entries.element.actions.element`, and the 4 ledgered for `ui/FormView` (root, `sections.element`, `subforms.element.columns.element`, `submitBehavior.options[1].url`) under `entries.element.form`. `kernel/MetadataTypeRegistryEntry` carries the same 8 under `actions.element`. Recounted from the file at this head: 275 entries, 1183 sites, matching the header. No refinement was written, weakened or removed; the ledger grows because two already-ledgered schemas are embedded, which is the admission the ledger asks to be made by hand.

### ② Semver level

- `.changeset/36887-meta-types-response-schema.md`: `@objectstack/spec` minor, `Clause-②: yes (widening: ...)`, `Metadata-protocol: added`. Both lines are line-initial in the changeset and in the PR body, and `Check Changeset` concluded success on this head.
- `Clause-②: yes (widening)` — right, with the unstated direction named in ① and N4.
- `Metadata-protocol: added` with `minor` — accepted. The spec's own ratchet counts every published schema key as authorable surface (`authorable-surface/api.json` lists `api/GetMetaTypesResponse:entries` and `:types`), four keys are added under `entries`, and #36881 declared the sibling `list` member the same way. One correction to the claim's stated reason: the `api` authorable-surface shard does NOT move in this diff, because that ratchet reads top-level keys only; the kind rests on the declaration, not on a moved baseline.
- Only `@objectstack/spec` publishes a change; `@objectstack/metadata-protocol` gains a test file and nothing shipped. Naming spec alone is right.
- `Skills-docs:` — owed by the kind and absent from the PR body. See N1. No skill teaching becomes false: `skills/objectstack-ui/SKILL.md:34` names `GET /api/v1/meta/types`, `entries[].schema` as the parsed shape served as JSON Schema, and the served bytes do not change. Nothing needs adding: `form`, `actions` and `schemaId` are Studio display data that only the spec registry and plugins produce, not something a metadata author writes.

### ③ Boundary flags

- `open_questions` in the dev report: empty. Nothing to answer.
- Dev flag, scope beyond the card's two named keys (`schemaId` and `actions` declared too, stated in claim 7127426588): answered, in scope. The card's Expected line is "declares every member the route serves", and its acceptance test, read strictly, cannot pass with two served members left undeclared.
- Dev flag, order ("with or after PR #36881"): #36881 is on `main` (`151e8123c2`); the diff adds beside its `list` member and does not touch it.
- Author: PR `user.login` is `objectstack-fleet[bot]`; no off-relay author to name.
- SQL push-down: the diff adds no data access, no id materialisation and no in-app join. The test's engine double is a stub that answers nothing.
- Security: none. No served byte changes; the schema declares members already on the wire.

### ④ Design judgment

`packages/spec/src/api/protocol.zod.ts` — holds against the code it cites and against the card.

- Card acceptance "declares `schema` and `form` with their real shapes, using the existing form-layout schema rather than `z.unknown()`": met. `form` is `FormViewSchema`; `schema` is a string-keyed record, and the spec has no narrower schema for a JSON Schema document.
- `form: FormViewSchema` (strict) against what is served: every served form is a `defineForm` output, which is `FormViewSchema.safeParse(...)` data bound to `data: { provider: 'schema', schemaId }`, so the wire carries a parsed form and a parsed form re-parses. Tried to break it through the translating door: `resolveMetadataFormLabels` (`packages/spec/src/system/i18n-resolver.ts`) writes only `label` and `description` on a section and `label`, `helpText`, `placeholder` on a field, each a string and each a declared key; for a `composite`, `repeater` or `record` field with no `fields` it synthesises children shaped `{ field, label?, helpText?, placeholder? }`, which `FormFieldSchema` accepts (`field` is its one required key, `fields` is declared on the recursive arm). `resolveMetadataFormSchemaTitles` returns an object, so `schema` stays a record. The strict member holds on both doors.
- `actions: ActionSchema[]` against plugin registrations: `registerMetadataTypeActions` does not parse what it is handed, so the schema is a promise the registry does not enforce. Read against the one production caller, `packages/services/service-datasource/src/datasource-admin-plugin.ts`: both actions (`test_connection`, `migrate_credential`) use `name`, `label`, `icon`, `type: 'api'`, `target`, `method: 'POST'`, `variant: 'secondary'`, `refreshAfter`, `locations` from `record_header` and `list_item`; every key is declared, every value is in its enum, `target` satisfies the api-type requirement, and none of the conditional refinements (`texts`, `refusals`, `outcomeMessages`, `preflight`) is engaged. The registry's own declarative `actions` are `ActionSchema` already (`MetadataTypeRegistryEntry.actions`). Holds.
- First consumer: the client SDK's `meta.getTypes()` returns `GetMetaTypesResponse` (`packages/client/src/index.ts`), so a typed caller now sees the four members; the console keeps its own entry type and is unaffected.

`packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.meta-types-response-schema-36887.test.ts` — agrees with the contract. It parses a `getMetaTypes()` answer after a JSON round-trip, covers every registry type plus the synthesised `webhook` arm, and reads "strict" as "no served key is stripped", which is the correct reading for a `z.object`. Both controls bite: an undeclared key is reported, and a malformed `form` is refused. See N3 for what it does not reach.

`packages/spec/src/type-alias-convention.pin.test.ts` and `packages/spec/dropped-refinements.baseline.json` — agree with the contract; judged in ①.

No must-fix, no should-fix.

- N1 (nit) — The PR body carries no `Skills-docs:` line, which `Metadata-protocol: added` owes. Prose face, no head move: add `Skills-docs: none — the declared members are Studio display data the spec registry and plugins produce, not something a metadata author writes; skills/objectstack-ui/SKILL.md:34 names entries[].schema only and stays true`. The L1 read lists a missing line as its own item.
- N2 (nit) — Two `describe` sentences are a little wider than the code. `form` says "labels in the request locale": true on the REST door, not on the runtime dispatcher door, which serves the registry's source labels (the `list` member on `main` already says the same). `schema` says "derived from its spec schema" in its first sentence while the second admits the hand-crafted source, and the REST door adds a translated `title` per node. Accepted deviation; a wording follow-up at most.
- N3 (nit) — The test parses the protocol answer, not the route's answer: the translated door (labels, and the synthesised `fields` children) is the one arm where a strict `form` could be broken later, and nothing pins it. Its plugin action is also a four-key reduction of the real datasource actions. Both arms hold by reading (④ above). Follow-up card: parse a `translateMetaTypesResponse` output with a bundle that names a child of a `repeater` field, and register the real plugin's two actions.
- N4 (nit) — The changeset and PR body say only "widening" and "nothing the server sends changes". They do not say that the schema now refuses an entry with no `schemaId`, or that a third-party `MetadataProtocol.getMetaTypes()` implementer returning `entries` must supply it to compile. No working caller is affected; accepted deviation.

## 席位核对 — REWORK · repo:objectstack#3 · head ce27cea1 · 2026-11-24T10:55Z

L1 read of #36948 (card #36887, p2, filed by triage and sized on its own) at `ce27cea1dfaba3cd3ca56c8ede2f6448505fabf2`. The contract-review record on this head reads **PASS** with no must-fix and no should-fix (7129413888). NOT governed (0 of 9 paths), 198 changed lines.

**The diff holds.** `GetMetaTypesResponseSchema` entries now declare `schemaId` (required), `schema` (a JSON-Schema record), `form` (`FormViewSchema`) and `actions` (`ActionSchema[]`). The last three are optional, matching `getMetaTypes`, which writes `schemaId` on both arms, can leave `schema` and `form` undefined, and spreads `actions` only when non-empty. Declaring `schemaId` and `actions` beyond the card's two named keys is in scope under the card's Expected line ("every member the route serves") and was stated in the claim. `GetMetaTypesResponseParsed` follows ADR-0122. The isomorphism pin leaves, with receipt, title and header all at 887. The 12 dropped-refinement entries are exactly the existing `ui/Action` (8) and `ui/FormView` (4) sites, re-prefixed. The test reads a real answer through JSON with a strict no-strip check, plus two controls (an undeclared key is reported, and a malformed `form` is refused). Clause-② `yes (widening)` and `Metadata-protocol: added` at `minor` match #36881's precedent for `list`.

**Changeset.** The one entry names `@objectstack/spec` at minor, and its sentences hold. The `l1-face` flag on `@objectstack/metadata-protocol` concerns a new test at `src/protocol.meta-types-response-schema-36887.test.ts` and the engine-double ledger, which lives under `scripts/`. The package's tsup entry is `src/index.ts` alone, with `files: ["dist", …]`, so the test is never bundled and no entry is owed.

**S1 (should-fix, PR body only, no head move).** `Metadata-protocol: added` owes a `Skills-docs:` line (os-dev's rule: any kind other than `none` adds the line). The body has none, so `l1-face` fails `skills-docs`. Add one line to the body, for example: `Skills-docs: none — the declared members are Studio display data the spec registry and plugins produce, not something a metadata author writes; skills/objectstack-ui/SKILL.md:34 names entries[].schema only and stays true`. The contract review confirms that value is true.

**Nits (no fix owed).** These are the contract review's N2–N4. N2: the `form` and `schema` describe lines are a little wider than the runtime door; `list` on main reads the same. N3: the synthesised-children arm and the full datasource actions are unpinned, and either can go to a follow-up card. N4: the changeset does not say that an `entries` implementer must now supply `schemaId`; no working caller is affected.

**Mechanical.** At read time: 25 success, 10 skipped, 32 in progress, 0 failed. All ten Test Core shards, Type Check · workspace and Build Core were not yet concluded.

**REWORK** on S1 alone. The delta is a body re-read plus `l1-face` on a green head; the head does not move, so the contract review stands.
